newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Merrill Lynch Swiss assets grow 51 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch Swiss assets grow 51 pct in 1996.

text.p: Merrill Lynch Bank Suisse said assets under management in Switzerland rose 51 percent in 1996 to 10.3 billion Swiss francs, including 4.0 billion Swiss francs in private assets under management which grew by 56 percent.

The bank's Geneva-based chairman Alfred Berger told a news conference in Zurich that Merrill Lynch Bank Suisse forecast a growth rate of between 20 and 25 percent in private client assets managed in Switzerland in 1997.
Assets under management in Switzerland were continuing to grow and totalled 11 billion Swiss francs at the end of February, he added.
Growth was attributed in part to market performance. Growth in new clients was 20 percent in 1996, Berger said.
The bank's 1996 earnings grew 30 percent to 43.3 million Swiss francs before taxes and provisions from 33.4 million in 1995.
Makram Zaccour, vice-chairman of Merrill Lynch International Bank Limited in London, told the same news conference: "We're growing in January and February at a much faster rate. We're bullish."
Merrill Lynch Bank Suisse has its headquarters in Geneva and two other offices in Zurich and Lugano and employs 134 staff.
The bank expects a 20 percent growth in private assets under management in the next five years globally.
Swiss banking estimates put the volume of private assets managed in Switzerland at up to $1.8 trillion.
